## Question 1

```{r q1}
(AAPL <- tq_get("AAPL", get = "stock.prices", from = "2015-01-01"))
```
\newpage

### 1. a.

```{r q1-a}
AAPL_with_dttm <- AAPL |>
  mutate(
    "dttm" = as_datetime(date)
  )
AAPL_with_dttm |>
  filter(date >= today() - dweeks(12)) |>
  ggplot(aes(dttm)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = pmin(close, open)), color = "gray") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = pmax(close, open), ymax = high), color = "gray") +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = dttm - dhours(10), xmax = dttm + dhours(10),
      ymin = pmin(close, open), ymax = pmax(close, open),
      fill = close >= open
    ),
    alpha = 0.80
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    breaks = c(FALSE,TRUE),
    values = c("firebrick", "forestgreen"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 weeks", date_labels = "%b %d") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Daily movement in AAPL share price over the past twelve weeks") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + 
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  )
```
\newpage

### 1. b.

```{r q1-b}
AAPL_by_week <- AAPL |>
  filter(year(date) == year(today())) |>
  group_by( week = week(date) ) |>
  arrange(date) |>
  summarize(
    date = date[1],
    open = open[1],
    close = close[n()],
    high = max(high),
    low = min(low)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
AAPL_by_week
```
\newpage

### 1. c.


### 1. d.

```{r q1-d}
AAPL_by_quarter <- AAPL |>
  group_by(
    year = year(date),
    quarter = quarter(date)
  ) |>
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarize(
    date = first(date),
    open = first(open),
    close = last(close),
    high = max(high),
    low = min(low),
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dttm = as_datetime(date)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(AAPL_by_quarter, aes(dttm)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = pmin(close, open)), color = "gray") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = pmax(close, open), ymax = high), color = "gray") +
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = dttm - dmonths(1),
      xmax = dttm + dmonths(1),
      ymin = pmin(close, open),
      ymax = pmax(close, open),
      fill = close >= open
    ),
    alpha = 0.80
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    breaks = c(FALSE, TRUE),
    values = c("firebrick", "forestgreen"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Quarterly movement in AAPL share price since 2015",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
\newpage

### 1. e.

```{r q1-e}
if ( fs::file_exists("SP500.rds") ) {
  SP500 <- read_rds("SP500.rds"); SP500_prices <- read_rds("SP500_prices.rds")
} else {
  SP500 <- tq_index("SP500"); write_rds(SP500, "SP500.rds")
  SP500_prices <- SP500 |> tq_get(get = "stock.prices", from = "2010-01-01")
  write_rds(SP500_prices, "SP500_prices.rds")}
SP500

SP500_prices
```

### 1. f.

```{r q1-f}
n_new <- SP500_prices |>
  summarize( first_day = min(date), .by = symbol) |>
  filter(first_day > mdy("Jan 4, 2010")) |>
  nrow()
n_total <- SP500_prices |>
  summarize( first_day = min(date), .by = symbol) |>
  nrow()
proportion <- n_new / n_total * 100

proportion
```

### 1. h.

```{r q1-h}
five_years_ago_trading_date <- today() - years(5)

seasoned_companies <- SP500_prices |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  summarize(
    first_date = min(date),
    last_date  = max(date),
  ) |>
  filter(
    first_date <= five_years_ago_trading_date,
    last_date  >= five_years_ago_trading_date
  ) |>
  pull(symbol)

sp_last_five_years <- SP500_prices |>
  filter(
    symbol %in% seasoned_companies,
    date >= five_years_ago_trading_date
  )
sp_last_five_years |> glimpse()
```
For question 1.h. ChatGPT5 helped me with creating seasoned_companies, and sp_last_five_years. Mainly with setting up filter and summarize in seasoned_companies, and with setting up filter in sp_last_five_years.
\newpage

### 1. i.

```{r q1-i}
sp_last_five_years_returns <- sp_last_five_years |>
  arrange(symbol, date) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  mutate(
    start_price = first(close),
    net_return = (close - start_price) / start_price
  ) |>
ggplot(sp_last_five_years_returns, aes(x = date, y = net_return, group = symbol)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Net returns over the last five years",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Net return since start date"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
For question 1.i. I used ChatGPT5 to help me create and format sp_last_five_years_returns, after that creating the graphic was simple enough by looking over the code provided in class for other parts. 
\newpage

### 1. j.

```{r q1-j}
sp_last_five_years_returns |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  summarize(final_return = last(net_return)) |>
  slice_max(final_return)
```
NVIDIA has had the greatest return over the last five years.

For this question, I used ChatGPT5 to help me find the most efficient way to find the highest return after grouping by symbol. Slice_max where recommended. Slice_max in particular was a great option because it allowed to select row with highest value.
